messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] switched alleles & multiple linkage groups
messages.body_plain:
Yes; in my experience, these switched alleles are due to genotyping errors.

The software looks for pairs of markers with associated genotypes (large LOD score for testing that the recombination fraction between them is not equal to 1/2), but with estimated recombination fraction > 1/2. (Near 1 rather than near 0.)

Gaps between markers should lead to rf ~ 1/2 and LOD ~ 0.

karl

messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] linkage map, gaps between markers
messages.body_plain:
With the Haldane map function, 50 cM corresponds to a recombination fraction of ~0.32; 100 cM corresponds to a rec frac of ~0.43.  With large data, you can have strong evidence for linkage even with 50 cM distances.

Also, if you use formLinkageGroups with restrictions min.lod but not on max.rf, you'll get markers placed into the same linkage group that have evidence of linkage but not be very tightly linked.

Or there could just be problems with marker order on that linkage group.

karl

messages.body_plain:
>From what I can see, what you need to do is the following:

  sex <- pull.pheno(q, "sex")
  male <- subset(q, ind=(sex==1))
  ac.male <- ac[sex==1,]
  out.m <- scanone(male, addcovar=ac.male)

A few comments on your code:

> > out.m <- scanone(subset(q, ind = sex==1),addcovar=ac[sex==1,])
> Error in subset.cross(q, ind = sex == 1) :
>   Must retain at least one individual.

The 'sex' vector must not be the same as pull.pheno(q, sex).

> > out.m <- scanone(subset(male, ind = sex==1),addcovar=ac[sex==1,])
> Error in subset.cross(male, ind = sex == 1) :
>   ind argument has wrong length (283; should be 138)

Since you'd already subseted by sex to create the 'male' dataset, you don't want to do it again here.

One last point: use caution in comparing the results of the separate analyses of males and females.  Evidence for a QTL in one sex and not the other doesn't mean that it is a sex-specific QTL. I avoid saying "sex-specific QTL" as much as possible, but instead focus on whether there is a sex-difference in the effect of the QTL (in other words, is there a QTL-by-sex interaction?). For that, you need to compare the model with sex as an interactive covariate to the model with sex as just an additive covariate.

karl

messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] correction for multiple testing
messages.body_plain:
If it's two or three phenotypes, I wouldn't correct for the multiple phenotypes.

If it's 10-20, I would control the family-wise error rate (FWER). See Burrage et al. Mamm Genome 21:115-129, 2010

  http://www.biostat.wisc.edu/~kbroman/publications/burrage.pdf

If it's >1,000 traits, I would either (1) don't control but be direct about what you did and about the chance of false positives, or (2) seek to control FDR across phenotypes (but still control the FWER for the scan across the genome).

karl

messages.body_plain:
The simplest approach is to use a common threshold for all phenotypes.

Then be sure that the permutations for the different phenotypes are conducted together in scanone, so that any correlations among phenotypes is preserved in the permutations:

  perms <- scanone(mycross, pheno.col = 1:nphe(mycross), n.perm=1000)

Then you just take the maximum across phenotypes:

  maxperms <- apply(perms, 1, max)

and then the quantile of this is your threshold:

  threshold <- quantile(maxperms, 0.95)

karl

messages.subject_clean: read.cross mapmaker format requires a genetic map
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

I have a bit of feedback.  This situation seems a little bit like a chicken or an egg problem.

I am in a course on QTL, but the data is from a real research project.  For course work we are hoping through a pile of popular software that has made it challenging to keep file formats straight.  A good intersection of software seems to handle mapmaker format including R/QTL.

At the moment, I am revisiting constructing a genetic map in the first place.  In particular I am examining evidence of segregation distortion in our data, so I dutifully sent out a csv of genotype information into mapmaker format, and loading it into R/QTL resulted in this:

qtl.data = read.cross(format="mm",dir=getwd(),file = "examine_full_original_genotype.raw", estimate.map=TRUE)
Error in read.cross.mm <http://read.cross.mm>(dir, file, mapfile, estimate.map) :
  Missing mapfile.

First my feed back:
This seems a bit unnecessary to require the map to even get started.  I want to use R/QTL prior to the construction of the map, and I wanted to use of the segregation distortion functions in R/QTL which have no particular dependence on a map.

One of the things I have wanted while working with onemap and R/QTL is the ability to skip the specific file format and just hand data.frame arguments with the information necessary to construct the required data.structures.  For example, I have written code to go from initial csvs to a csv format that R/QTL wants and then I load them in via read.cross, but that seems a little "round about".  Why not just expose an interface to provide the data as data.frames instead of files?

I thought about constructing a bogus map file to trip R/QTL into loading the data.   Is there an option that I am missing that will make R/QTL run without a map from mapmaker files?

Anyway, thanks for the software and listening.

sup6 <- calc.genoprob(data2, step=10)

out <- scanone(sup2)

Likewise running

I also tried the imputation method on my data

sug8 <- sim.geno(data2, n.draws=100)

which also gave me the same output.

Any idea what is going on?
